newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Wednesday in line with LME copper as the market continued to slide during the seasonally slow summer period, analysts said.
COMEX September copper was called down 0.50 to 1.00 cent from Tuesday's close of 105.05 cents a lb after trading between 105.40 and 103.90 on ACCESS.
LME copper stocks rose 975 tonnes to 134,325 tonnes in Wednesday's data, while COMEX copper stocks fell 1,547 short tons to 39,722 short tons Tuesday.

While the LME cash-to-three month spread remains relatively firm around $124.00 a tonne, the COMEX September/December spread has slid sharply in the past 10 days to 1.90 cents from a high over 5.00 cents in late June, reflecting fears a supply/demand surplus may emerge in late 1997 as originally forecast.
Meanwhile, the copper market continues to shrug off a continuing strike at the Neves Corvo copper mine in Portugal.
